profile.reading:
CoreSite VA2 is the second and, by the operator's own published square footage, the smallest of the three buildings on CoreSite's Reston, Virginia campus, addressed at 12098 Sunrise Valley Drive per CoreSite's own facility page, immediately adjacent to the larger VA1 building at 12100 Sunrise Valley Drive. The Reston campus, formerly Sunrise Technology Park, sits on a 21.73 acre tract in Fairfax County's Hunter Mill District. Fairfax County planning commission records show CoreSite Real Estate Sunrise Technology Park LLC brought rezoning case RZ 2017-HM-032 and special exception case SE 2017-HM-030 covering this same tract before the Planning Commission on June 28, 2018, where the related motions carried unanimously 10 to 0 with two commissioners recused, and the Board of Supervisors gave final approval on July 31, 2018, described by the county's own public affairs office as the first approval under new provisions meant to more easily allow data centers into Fairfax County. That approval covered the whole campus, VA2 included, converting roughly 463,212 square feet of 1980s office space, formerly an AOL office campus that Boston Properties sold in 2016 for 60 million dollars, into an eventual six building, four phase buildout the operator's spec sheet page puts at more than 1.3 million square feet at full build out. The case raised the site's floor area ratio from 0.5 to 0.99 and required LEED Silver certification campus wide.

CoreSite's own dedicated facility page for VA2 publishes more than 192,000 square feet for this building specifically, its only quantitative figure beyond the address, and the operator's separate VA2 spec sheet page adds no further detail. No megawatt capacity, standby generation figure, or opening year specific to VA2 is published anywhere on CoreSite's site, and no reliable secondary figure was found either, so none of the four power numbers this registry tracks are asserted for VA2. CoreSite lists SOC 1 Type 2, SOC 2 Type 2, ISO 27001, NIST 800-53, PCI DSS, and HIPAA compliance across its facilities generally, without specifying which certifications apply building by building.

Fairfax County's tax department sought tenant identity and contact information covering what a March 2024 filing described as four data centers and an office building at the adjoining 12100 Sunrise Valley Drive address, and CoreSite sued the county on March 8, 2024 rather than comply, a dispute that per Data Center Dynamics remained unresolved in court as of the report consulted, though that filing named the VA1 address rather than VA2's own. Separately, in November 2026 the Virginia State Corporation Commission approved new Dominion Energy rates creating a GS-5 data center rate class effective January 1, 2027, requiring 14 year mandatory contracts for facilities with 25 megawatts or more of demand, per Inside Climate News, a change that will bear on this campus's power arrangements even though VA2's own load remains unpublished. Parent company American Tower separately reported record CoreSite leasing and a raised 2026 outlook projecting 1.20 to 1.22 billion dollars in data center segment revenue, funding continued build out across CoreSite's markets including this Reston campus. Fairfax County's Board of Supervisors also directed staff on March 19, 2024 to draft stricter data center zoning standards for future projects, covering residential buffers, noise studies, and a shift from by right to special exception approval, though FFXnow reported that CoreSite's already approved Reston buildout, VA2 included, is grandfathered out of those newer 2024 rules.

profile.community_note: No organized resident opposition specific to VA2 was found in this research, in contrast to the newer V3 phase at 12367 Sunrise Valley Drive on the same broader campus, where FFXnow reported nearby Cocquina Cluster homeowners raising height, noise, traffic, light, and cooling tower steam concerns in 2025.
profile.regulatory_note: Fairfax County approved the whole Reston campus, VA2 included, under rezoning case RZ 2017-HM-032 and special exception SE 2017-HM-030 on July 31, 2018, described by the county as its first approval under new provisions favoring data centers. A related 2024 dispute over Fairfax County's tenant identity records request named the adjoining VA1 address specifically, and CoreSite sued the county over that request on March 8, 2024, unresolved as of the report reviewed. More restrictive countywide data center zoning standards the Board directed staff to draft on March 19, 2024 do not apply retroactively to this already approved campus.

reading.body:
CoreSite VA2 Reston is a 192,000 square foot building on a 21.73 acre campus in Fairfax County that Fairfax County approved for data center conversion in 2018 under rezoning case RZ 2017-HM-032, the county's first approval under provisions designed to favor data centers. The operator publishes no megawatt capacity, standby generation, or opening year specific to this building, making its current power draw and future scaling potential unknown. CoreSite's broader Reston campus, including VA2, is grandfathered out of more restrictive zoning standards the county directed staff to draft in March 2024 and represents part of what American Tower's parent company reported as record leasing across CoreSite's markets in 2026.

The building holds SOC 1 Type 2, SOC 2 Type 2, and ISO 27001 certifications for information security governance; NIST 800-53 and PCI DSS compliance; and HIPAA eligibility for regulated healthcare workloads. Virginia's November 2026 regulatory approval of new data center electric rates effective January 1, 2027 will affect this campus's power arrangements if VA2 or the Reston campus as a whole draws 25 megawatts or more, requiring 14 year mandatory contracts for qualifying facilities, though VA2's own load remains unpublished.

Virginia publishes capacity figures for only 25 of 330 mapped data center facilities in the state, totaling 1,603.4 megawatts. Because CoreSite does not publish VA2's power consumption, this facility cannot be ranked within Virginia's operating capacity. The adjoining VA1 building was the subject of a March 2024 legal dispute over tenant identity between CoreSite and Fairfax County, which remains unresolved, leaving the occupancy and power utilization of the Reston campus as a whole outside public record.
